narrative:
At the checkpoint, Mara finds her rival, Iven, named on the arrest ledger for the fire she helped start. The evidence is thin but sufficient: a scorched seal, three witnesses, and the patrol captain’s need to make an example before nightfall. Iven sees Mara among the petitioners and understands at once that she can contradict the report. He also knows what that would cost her. Neither of them says the word sorry.

Mara steps forward only when the captain reaches for the shackles. She offers the iron signet she inherited from the governor’s office, claiming it as surety for Iven’s appearance at dawn. It is the one possession that can clear her passage through the city and expose her connection to the fire if the captain examines its hidden mark. Her hand shakes once; she closes it around the ring until the tremor stops.

“Keep him,” she says, with restrained dryness, “if you prefer a prisoner who can’t lead you to the missing ledger.” It is a lie, but a useful one. She bargains Iven’s freedom against his knowledge of the ledger’s route, placing both of them under the captain’s scrutiny. Iven resists—not from pride, but because accepting her protection would make him appear complicit. He counters that he will guide the patrol only if Mara comes as guarantor. His refusal forces her to choose publicly rather than rescue him secretly.

Mara agrees, surrendering the signet and her safe status. In return, Iven names a false meeting place that buys them until dawn, but he does not absolve her or deny what he suspects. The captain releases him under conditional watch. As they leave, Iven returns Mara’s glove, which he had taken from the burned building. She accepts it without looking at him.

“Payment,” he says.

“For the trouble?”

“For the bargain.”

The exchange is an apology only in shape: each acknowledges the harm without confessing guilt. Their distrust remains intact, but Iven now chooses to walk beside her rather than away. Mara has protected the person most capable of exposing her, and the cost has made her concealed loyalty impossible to dismiss.
title: The Price of a Partial Mercy
